subject.title: Proposal: safer self-update with pre-update backup + health check + auto-rollback/restore

question: Should OpenClaw own an integrated core safe-update transaction, and what rollback, state-restore, smoke-check, retention, and secret-handling policy should that transaction use?
rationale: The remaining work crosses core updater behavior, backup/restore semantics, live smoke criteria, credentials/state handling, and overlapping update/backup issues, so automation cannot choose the product and security boundary safely.

options.title: Design Core Safe Update
options.body: Keep #14526 as the umbrella and specify a narrow opt-in core updater mode that orchestrates existing primitives with explicit rollback and restore policy.

options.title: Split Into Narrower Work
options.body: Move implementation into linked backup/restore, scanner, external-updater, and auto-update issues, leaving #14526 as product tracking only.

options.title: Reject Automatic Restore
options.body: Keep manual backup and rollback docs only if maintainers decide automatic state restore is too risky for core.

recommendation.title: Design Core Safe Update
recommendation.body: Keep #14526 as the umbrella and specify a narrow opt-in core updater mode that orchestrates existing primitives with explicit rollback and restore policy.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already provided the relevant keep-open product-scope review and is tied to current update/backup source history.
